Alice M: Ran an nsys capture on the KV-prefetch path and the timeline looks like memcpy (host->device) on stream 0 serializing multiple kernels. attaching screenshot + trace link: s3://ci-traces/1812345678/nsys.zip
Ben R: Can you paste the nsys CLI you used? and which CUDA version?
Alice M: `nsys profile --output=kvprefetch --capture-range=nvtx --trace=cuda,nvtx,osrt --sample=none python -u run_trace.py` (CUDA 12.1)
Carla S: Quick guess: are we using pageable host buffers? if memcpy is falling back to blocking path it'll go through the legacy stream and force serialization. were buffers allocated with cudaHostAlloc / pinned alloc? :thinking:
Alice M: Nope, currently we malloc for KV staging then cudaMemcpyAsync(dst, src, size, cudaMemcpyHostToDevice, stream) from runtime thread pool. I assumed async would be fine.
Carla S: The catch: cudaMemcpyAsync from Pageable memory is synchronous w.r.t. host and acts like a blocking copy. Use pinned host memory (cudaHostAlloc) or use gpuDirect staging. Also ensure kernels are launched to non-default streams. Legacy default stream semantics can serialize even if you use streams.
infra-bot: trace uploaded to s3://ci-traces/1812345678/nsys.zip (sha256: abcd...)
